findings.text: the landed record cites the gate revision as f8f6617, which is not an object in the repository (git cat-file -t exits 128) while logs/gate_new_test.log names f8f36b76, so a reader checking the record opens a revision that does not exist.

the expected attach line was replaced by a fresh call to the composer under test, so this assertion and the regression it names now move together: restoring the bare word leaves it green and only the new gate file reddens.
the same substitution leaves the recorded waiver compared against the composer's own output, so the file pins no behaviour of the line it names.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit; f8f36b76 changes only runs.py plus three test files, and f2a036e3 adds the plan landed record (39 insertions) and a new evidence file (88 insertions) with no rewrites.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when's first three clauses are asserted by tests/test_attach_line_resolves.py (absolute path, executable file, token run as `crew follow --help` under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin requiring exit 0, plus the refusal), and its last two are recorded in the manifest's logs; the clause that every existing test asserting on the attach line text still passes holds over the two granted fixture files only, the two out-of-scope assertions being red at the head and named in follow_ons.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that the follower attach line names the absolute path of the running reckon entry point; reckon/crew/runs.py:2452 composes its first token through _reckon_console_script (runs.py:1992), and my own re-run of the gate showed the composed token is the executable virtualenv console script.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the gate as 2 passed at f8f36b76 with its log, added failures 0 against the base logs, and the executed negative control, and its two follow-ons match the stale literals I read at tests/test_crew_session_delivery.py:223 and tests/test_crew.py:1887.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the seven declared paths fence reckon/crew/runs.py, three test files and two docs; the diff d6817708..f2a036e3 touches six files and every one is inside them.

justifications.durability: tests/test_attach_line_resolves.py fails on the declared regression, executed and logged red; but tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py:253 and tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py:165 now compare against a re-call of the composer, so a composer regression leaves them green.
justifications.evidence: logs/gate_new_test.log names revision f8f36b76, tree and command, the before/after logs reproduce the same five failures (added failures 0), and negative_control.log reds the gate at PYTEST_EXIT=1; the residual is that the landed record's revision citation and the two red out-of-scope assertions are named rather than measured green.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/runs.py:1992 names the helper for what it returns, is shared by both callers, and its docstring states the symlink reason for dropping .resolve(); the tests follow the file's monkeypatch idiom.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/runs.py:1992 returns the running interpreter's sibling without resolving the virtualenv symlink away, and my re-run of tests/test_attach_line_resolves.py composed a first token that is the venv's executable console script.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff of d6817708..f2a036e3 changes six files, all inside the seven declared write paths, and the two out-of-scope attach-line literals were left untouched as the fence required.
